angleRead.name: Trevor Shimizu
angleRead.text: I've been watching the Temescal civic initiative stall out, same as Fruitvale's did before it. Makes me wonder if there's a pattern in how these neighborhood projects lose steam. I'll start by checking in with the usual community contacts - Sonia, Idris, Sam - see if they've noticed anything specific holding things up this cycle. Maybe compare notes with what happened in Fruitvale.

I'll start by checking in with the usual community contacts - Sonia, Idris, Sam - see if they've noticed anything specific holding things up this cycle. plan.focus: Identifying common factors in stalled civic initiatives across Oakland neighborhoods.
plan.why: Noticing parallel stagnation in Temescal and Fruitvale initiatives suggests systemic rather than localized issues.
checks: Verify if same agencies/processes are involved in both initiatives
Compare timeline patterns between the two stalled projects
Check for overlapping community concerns or opposition

targets.question: Have you observed any specific roadblocks to the Temescal initiative this cycle?
Are there procedural similarities between the current Temescal stall and what happened in Fruitvale?
What's the community sentiment about the initiative's lack of progress?

plan.interpretation: Recurring initiative stagnation may indicate systemic bottlenecks in Oakland's civic approval processes.
unverifiedLead: Potential resource allocation disparities between neighborhoods
Possible changes in municipal review timelines
plan.closeQuestion: Are we seeing a citywide pattern of neighborhood initiatives getting stuck at the same stage?
